QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_8

question.text: The 'Catch-up' clause in a Category II AIF waterfall specifies that:

answer.text: The manager is allocated residual profits after hurdle is paid, until the manager reaches its pre-determined share of total profits
The manager receives 100% of management fees retrospectively for missed years
Investors catch up on deferred distributions at fund wind-up
GST on management fees is collected in a lump sum at fund termination

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Ch 9.3.1: Catch-up is the rate at which residual profits (after capital return and hurdle) are allocated to the Manager so the Manager 'catches up' to its pre-agreed share of TOTAL profits (say 20%). A 100% catch-up means ALL residual after hurdle goes to GP until the target share is met. **The Trap:** Option B is a made-up construct. Option C reverses the beneficiary of catch-up. Option D is an unrelated tax mechanic. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-A/B tests this from LP side; XIX-C tests the computation and negotiation. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Catch-up rates are a key negotiation lever. A 50% catch-up splits the post-hurdle residual equally between GP catching up and LPs, extending the time before GP reaches target share — LPs prefer this because they see cash sooner.
